tasks.label: Install the standard on this machine
tasks.help: Installs the rules block + hooks and creates your page index (the Notion database the audit uses to catalog your pages). One-time. The page index has a required structure, so the standard creates it — it's never a pasted link.

groups.name: Locations
groups.help: The Notion pages the tool uses. Paste a link if you have one, or use the create option under a field to make one.

settings.label: Catch-all page
settings.help: Where a page goes when it doesn't clearly belong anywhere else — your safe default (for example a general Notes or Projects space).

settings.label: Audit results page
settings.help: Where a scheduled audit posts its findings. Not needed if you only run the audit by hand.

settings.label: Default home per page type
settings.help: Optional — skip if unsure. The page types are the six modes from your Recording Standard. For a given type, set the default place a new page of that type goes when it has no obvious parent: pick the type and paste the home page's link.

settings.label: Custom routing rules
settings.help: Optional. Plain-English rules, one per line, for where your own pages should go — for example: 'When an idea gets a design doc, move it to Project Wikis.' Stored as text in your config; the audit job reads and applies them on each run. Leave blank for none.

tasks.label: Create the audit results page
tasks.help: Makes the page and fills this in.

settings.label: How often to audit (days)
settings.help: Number of days between automatic audits.

settings.label: What to check
settings.help: 'incremental' checks only pages changed since the last audit (cheaper); 'full' checks every page.

settings.label: How much to fix automatically
settings.help: What the audit changes on its own versus only suggests. It never deletes, and always logs what it changed.

tasks.label: Schedule the audit to run automatically
tasks.help: Sets up the recurring audit at the cadence above. Skip this if you prefer to run the audit by hand.
